title: Enhance ArazzoRunner to support URL-based Arazzo docs, nested workflows, and direct operation execution

raw.title: Enhance ArazzoRunner to support URL-based Arazzo docs, nested workflows, and direct operation execution
raw.body:
Summary

This PR enhances the ArazzoRunner to provide:

Support for loading Arazzo documents from URLs (http:// or https://).

Execution of nested workflows with proper parameter evaluation and outputs propagation.

Direct operation execution outside of workflows via execute_operation.

Improved environment variable mappings via the new static method generate_env_mappings.

Preservation of deprecated get_env_mappings with warnings for backward compatibility.

All changes are implemented with minimal refactoring and no deletion of existing documentation/comments.

Changes Made

Added URL support for loading .json, .yaml, and .yml Arazzo documents.

Nested workflow execution _execute_nested_workflow with expression evaluation for parameters.

execute_operation method to execute individual API operations directly.

Added generate_env_mappings static method for auth and server environment variables.

Deprecated get_env_mappings now points users to generate_env_mappings.

Maintained existing event callbacks and logging for steps and workflows.

Copilot Review:

Key Changes
1. Remote URL Support for Workflow and Source Files
runner/arazzo_runner/runner.py

The runner can now load an Arazzo workflow document from a remote URL (http://, https://).
When a URL is detected, it fetches the content via HTTP, detects the format (YAML/JSON), and parses accordingly.
On error, a clear ValueError is raised.
runner/arazzo_runner/utils.py

Refactored file loading into a generic load_file() that handles both YAML and JSON, with improved error handling.
load_source_descriptions() now supports loading OpenAPI/source files from both local paths and remote URLs.
For local files, multiple candidate paths are checked; for remote files, HTTP GET is used and format is detected via Content-Type.
2. Utility and Typing Improvements
Improved type hints and function signatures for better maintainability.
Consolidated environment variable sanitization and naming logic.
Logging is now more consistent and uses a dedicated logger ("runner-utils").
3. Test Suite Enhancements
runner/tests/test_arazzo_runner.py
The test runner now includes cases for loading workflow and source files from remote URLs.
The mock HTTP client (MockHTTPExecutor) is improved: supports headers, params, and simulates responses more closely to actual HTTP clients.
Test cases validate that requests are correctly formed, including payloads and headers.
New tests check that remote workflow and source loading works as intended.
4. Code Cleanup and Refactoring
Old or redundant utility functions (e.g., repeated file loaders, unnecessary openapi loader) have been removed or consolidated.
Docstrings and comments are updated for clarity.
Strengths
Extensibility: Adds remote loading capability, making Arazzo workflows and API specs easier to share and reuse.
Robustness: Improved error messages and file searching logic for sources.
Maintainability: Refactored utilities and better typing make future changes easier.
Testing: The new tests ensure both local and remote loading paths are covered.
Suggestions & Questions
Error Handling:

In load_source_descriptions, if all candidate paths fail, a FileNotFoundError is raised. Consider logging all candidate paths for easier debugging.
For remote sources, YAML is detected via Content-Type containing "yaml" or "yml". If the server returns application/octet-stream or no type, fallback detection might be useful.
MockHTTPExecutor:

The mock HTTP client is well-implemented. For advanced scenarios, consider simulating timeouts or network errors.
Backward Compatibility:

The utility refactor removes some legacy functions. If other parts of the codebase rely on them, a migration plan might be needed.
Documentation:

The API for remote file loading is intuitive, but updating the main README with examples would benefit users.
Summary
This PR is a solid improvement: it adds much-needed remote file loading, cleans up utilities, and improves test coverage.
There are no critical blockers. Minor improvements to error handling and documentation would further strengthen this update.
